newsitem.title: GREECE: AGRICULTURAL BANK LAUNCHES NEW HOUSING LOAN PROGRAMME.
newsitem.headline: AGRICULTURAL BANK LAUNCHES NEW HOUSING LOAN PROGRAMME.

text.p: Agricultural Bank of Greece is launching new housing loans, its governor Christos Papathanasiou announced on Wednesday.
"The loans are available for the purchase, completion, expansion and repair of a home and may be taken up to finance land purchases as well," the bank said in a statement.
Borrowers may choose between a fixed or floating rate loan.
Fixed-rate loans feature a rate of 11.0 percent for the first three years when instalments are monthly and 12.0 percent for quarterly payments.
Likewise, floating-rate loans are available at 13.0 percent for monthly payments and at 14.0 percent for quarterly payments.
Maturities may go as far as 15 years and may feature a 12-month grace period. The loans may finance up to 70 percent of the real estate, the bank said.
Borrowers are insured at no extra charge by Agricultural Bank's subsidiary Agrotiki Insurance against personal accidents. --George Georgiopoulos, Athens Newsroom +301 3311812-4
